en: Earth's seasons are caused by its 23.5-degree axial tilt, not by Earth's changing distance from the Sun.
Moon phases occur because we see different amounts of the Moon's sunlit half as it orbits Earth, not because Earth's shadow falls on the Moon.
Clouds are made of millions of tiny liquid water droplets or ice crystals, not of invisible water vapor.
Stars remain in the sky during daytime, but the Sun's bright scattered light makes them invisible to the naked eye.
Topsoil is the most fertile soil layer because it contains the highest concentration of humus from decomposed plants and animals.
A mineral is a naturally formed solid with a specific chemical composition and crystal structure, while a rock is made of one or more minerals.
About 68.7 percent of Earth's fresh water is frozen in glaciers and ice caps, not stored in rivers or lakes.
A meteor is the bright streak of light produced when a space rock burns up in Earth's atmosphere, not the rock itself.
Earthquakes occur when built-up stress causes rocks along a fault line to suddenly break and slip, releasing energy as seismic waves.
Wind blows because the Sun heats Earth's surface unevenly, causing warm air to rise and cooler air to rush in and replace it.
Obsidian is an igneous rock that forms when lava cools so rapidly that no crystals can form, creating a smooth glassy texture.
Venus is the hottest planet in the solar system because its thick carbon dioxide atmosphere traps heat, even though Mercury is closer to the Sun.
